verses.sanskrit: ईशा वास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् | तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ||
verses.transliteration: īśā vāsyamidaṃ sarvaṃ yatkiñca jagatyāṃ jagat | tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasviddhanam ||
verses.translation: Whatever exists in this changing world is pervaded by the Lord. Through detachment (renunciation) enjoy what comes. Do not covet anyone's wealth.
verses.hindi: इस गतिशील जगत में जो कुछ भी है, वह सब ईश्वर से आच्छादित है। उसका त्याग (अनासक्ति) के साथ भोग करो। किसी के धन की लालसा मत करो।
verses.commentary: The opening mantra establishes the entire philosophy: everything is pervaded by the divine, therefore nothing is privately owned. Enjoyment without grasping; engagement without attachment. This is karma-yoga in a single line.
verses.wordMeaning: The opening mantra establishes the entire philosophy: everything is pervaded by the divine, therefore nothing is privately owned. Enjoyment without grasping; engagement without attachment. This is karma-yoga in a single line.

verses.sanskrit: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः | एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ||
verses.transliteration: kurvanneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ | evaṃ tvayi nānyatheto'sti na karma lipyate nare ||
verses.translation: Performing actions here, one should desire to live a hundred years. There is no other way — action does not bind a man who lives thus.
verses.hindi: यहाँ कर्म करते हुए ही व्यक्ति सौ वर्ष जीने की इच्छा करे। तेरे लिये इसके अतिरिक्त कोई और मार्ग नहीं है; ऐसे जीने वाले मनुष्य को कर्म लिप्त नहीं करते।
verses.commentary: A radical correction to world-renouncing tendencies: the Upanishad explicitly endorses a hundred-year life of action. The secret is not to flee karma but to act without ego-attachment. Action then becomes non-binding.
verses.wordMeaning: A radical correction to world-renouncing tendencies: the Upanishad explicitly endorses a hundred-year life of action. The secret is not to flee karma but to act without ego-attachment. Action then becomes non-binding.

verses.sanskrit: असुर्या नाम ते लोका अन्धेन तमसाऽऽवृताः | तांस्ते प्रेत्याभिगच्छन्ति ये के चात्महनो जनाः ||
verses.transliteration: asuryā nāma te lokā andhena tamasā''vṛtāḥ | tāṃste pretyābhigacchanti ye ke cātmahano janāḥ ||
verses.translation: There are worlds called "asurya" (demonic, sunless), enveloped in blinding darkness. Those who slay the Self go there after death.
verses.hindi: वे लोक "असुर्य" (सूर्य-रहित, अन्धकारमय) कहलाते हैं और घोर अन्धकार से ढके हैं। जो लोग आत्म-हन्ता हैं, वे मृत्यु के बाद उन्हीं लोकों में जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: A stern warning. To "kill the Self" (ātma-han) is to live as though you were only the body — to ignore the spiritual dimension. Such a life leads, the Upanishad says, to a state of darkness here and hereafter. Materialism is described as a kind of suicide.
verses.wordMeaning: A stern warning. To "kill the Self" (ātma-han) is to live as though you were only the body — to ignore the spiritual dimension. Such a life leads, the Upanishad says, to a state of darkness here and hereafter. Materialism is described as a kind of suicide.

verses.sanskrit: अनेजदेकं मनसो जवीयो नैनद्देवा आप्नुवन् पूर्वमर्षत् | तद्धावतोऽन्यानत्येति तिष्ठत् तस्मिन्नपो मातरिश्वा दधाति ||
verses.transliteration: anejadekaṃ manaso javīyo nainaddevā āpnuvan pūrvamarṣat | taddhāvato'nyānatyeti tiṣṭhat tasminnapo mātariśvā dadhāti ||
verses.translation: Unmoving, one, swifter than the mind — the senses cannot reach It, for It moves ahead of them. Standing still, It outruns those who run. In It the cosmic wind sustains all activity.
verses.hindi: वह अचल है, एक है, मन से भी तेज है। इन्द्रियाँ उसे नहीं पकड़ सकतीं, क्योंकि वह उनसे पहले ही पहुँच जाता है। स्थिर रहकर वह दौड़ने वालों से आगे निकल जाता है। उसी में मातरिश्वा (वायु) सबकी क्रियाओं को धारण करता है।
verses.commentary: The Self is paradoxical — unmoving yet swifter than mind. It is the substratum in which all movement occurs, never moving itself. Like the screen of a film: the screen never moves, yet every motion appears on it.
verses.wordMeaning: The Self is paradoxical — unmoving yet swifter than mind. It is the substratum in which all movement occurs, never moving itself. Like the screen of a film: the screen never moves, yet every motion appears on it.

verses.sanskrit: तदेजति तन्नैजति तद्दूरे तद्वन्तिके | तदन्तरस्य सर्वस्य तदु सर्वस्यास्य बाह्यतः ||
verses.transliteration: tadejati tannaijati taddūre tadvantike | tadantarasya sarvasya tadu sarvasyāsya bāhyataḥ ||
verses.translation: It moves, and It moves not. It is far, and It is near. It is within all this, and It is outside of all this.
verses.hindi: वह चलता है और नहीं भी चलता। वह दूर है और पास भी। वह इन सब के भीतर है और इन सब के बाहर भी।
verses.commentary: Immanence and transcendence in one breath. The Self is the inner-most of all and yet beyond everything. Distance is a category of mind; the Self is closer than your jugular and farther than the stars.
verses.wordMeaning: Immanence and transcendence in one breath. The Self is the inner-most of all and yet beyond everything. Distance is a category of mind; the Self is closer than your jugular and farther than the stars.

verses.sanskrit: यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्येवानुपश्यति | सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विजुगुप्सते ||
verses.transliteration: yastu sarvāṇi bhūtānyātmanyevānupaśyati | sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ tato na vijugupsate ||
verses.translation: He who sees all beings in the Self, and the Self in all beings — he no longer feels aversion toward anything.
verses.hindi: जो सभी प्राणियों को आत्मा में देखता है, और सभी प्राणियों में आत्मा को देखता है — वह फिर किसी से घृणा नहीं करता।
verses.commentary: The ethical conclusion of non-duality: when the Self is seen as the common substance of all beings, aversion becomes impossible. You cannot hate what you recognize as yourself. Compassion is not a moral effort — it is the natural consequence of clear seeing.
verses.wordMeaning: The ethical conclusion of non-duality: when the Self is seen as the common substance of all beings, aversion becomes impossible. You cannot hate what you recognize as yourself. Compassion is not a moral effort — it is the natural consequence of clear seeing.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मैवाभूद् विजानतः | तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वमनुपश्यतः ||
verses.transliteration: yasmin sarvāṇi bhūtānyātmaivābhūd vijānataḥ | tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ ||
verses.translation: When, for the knower, all beings have become the Self alone — what delusion, what sorrow can there be for one who sees this oneness?
verses.hindi: ज्ञानी पुरुष के लिये जब सभी प्राणी आत्मा ही हो गए हों — एकत्व देखने वाले को फिर मोह कैसा, शोक कैसा?
verses.commentary: Sorrow requires a separate "other" to lose. Delusion requires a separate "self" to be confused. When the seer recognizes one undivided Self pervading all, both vanish at the root. This is liberation in life.
verses.wordMeaning: Sorrow requires a separate "other" to lose. Delusion requires a separate "self" to be confused. When the seer recognizes one undivided Self pervading all, both vanish at the root. This is liberation in life.

verses.sanskrit: स पर्यगाच्छुक्रमकायमव्रणमस्नाविरं शुद्धमपापविद्धम् | कविर्मनीषी परिभूः स्वयम्भूर्याथातथ्यतोऽर्थान् व्यदधाच्छाश्वतीभ्यः समाभ्यः ||
verses.transliteration: sa paryagācchukramakāyamavraṇamasnāviraṃ śuddhamapāpaviddham | kavirmanīṣī paribhūḥ svayambhūryāthātathyato'rthān vyadadhācchāśvatībhyaḥ samābhyaḥ ||
verses.translation: He has reached all — bright, bodiless, woundless, sinewless, pure, untouched by evil; seer, wise, all-encompassing, self-existent — distributing things according to their nature, for endless years.
verses.hindi: वह सर्वव्यापी है — दीप्तिमान, अशरीर, क्षत-रहित, स्नायु-रहित, शुद्ध, पाप-रहित; कवि, मनीषी, सर्वव्यापी, स्वयम्भू; अनन्त वर्षों तक यथार्थ-रूप से सबको उसकी प्रकृति के अनुसार व्यवस्थित करता है।
verses.commentary: The most poetic mantra of the Upanishad — a cascade of attributes describing the Self/Brahman. Not 'sketchy' qualities but a precise spiritual phenomenology: brilliant, beyond body, beyond injury, beyond moral stain; the inner seer who orders all things according to their nature.
verses.wordMeaning: The most poetic mantra of the Upanishad — a cascade of attributes describing the Self/Brahman. Not 'sketchy' qualities but a precise spiritual phenomenology: brilliant, beyond body, beyond injury, beyond moral stain; the inner seer who orders all things according to their nature.

verses.sanskrit: अन्धं तमः प्रविशन्ति येऽविद्यामुपासते | ततो भूय इव ते तमो य उ विद्यायां रताः ||
verses.transliteration: andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye'vidyāmupāsate | tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u vidyāyāṃ ratāḥ ||
verses.translation: Those who worship ignorance enter blinding darkness. Those who delight only in knowledge enter into darkness deeper still.
verses.hindi: जो अविद्या (कर्मकाण्ड, लौकिक ज्ञान) की ही उपासना करते हैं, वे अन्धकार में प्रवेश करते हैं। जो केवल विद्या में ही रमण करते हैं, वे उससे भी अधिक अन्धकार में उतरते हैं।
verses.commentary: Ritual without understanding is blindness; book-knowledge without practice is a deeper blindness. The verse anticipates the modern danger of the over-educated person who knows everything in theory and nothing in life.
verses.wordMeaning: Ritual without understanding is blindness; book-knowledge without practice is a deeper blindness. The verse anticipates the modern danger of the over-educated person who knows everything in theory and nothing in life.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यदेवाहुर्विद्ययाऽन्यदाहुरविद्यया | इति शुश्रुम धीराणां ये नस्तद्विचचक्षिरे ||
verses.transliteration: anyadevāhurvidyayā'nyadāhuravidyayā | iti śuśruma dhīrāṇāṃ ye nastadvicacakṣire ||
verses.translation: Knowledge yields one fruit, they say; ignorance yields another. So we have heard from the wise who explained these to us.
verses.hindi: विद्या से एक फल कहा गया है और अविद्या से अन्य — ऐसा हमने उन धीर पुरुषों से सुना है जिन्होंने हमें यह समझाया।
verses.commentary: Knowledge (vidyā, Self-knowledge) and ignorance (avidyā, here meaning ritual/karmic action) bear different fruits. This bridge verse prepares the famous next mantra: that both must be united for true liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: Knowledge (vidyā, Self-knowledge) and ignorance (avidyā, here meaning ritual/karmic action) bear different fruits. This bridge verse prepares the famous next mantra: that both must be united for true liberation.

verses.sanskrit: विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह | अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते ||
verses.transliteration: vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ca yastadvedobhayaṃ saha | avidyayā mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā vidyayā'mṛtamaśnute ||
verses.translation: He who knows both vidyā and avidyā together crosses death through avidyā and attains immortality through vidyā.
verses.hindi: जो विद्या और अविद्या — दोनों को एक साथ जानता है, वह अविद्या से मृत्यु को पार करता है और विद्या से अमरत्व प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The synthesis. Ritual, action, ethical living (avidyā in this technical sense) carry one across the river of birth-and-death; Self-knowledge (vidyā) confers immortality. Both are needed: world-engagement and inward realization, not one or the other.
verses.wordMeaning: The synthesis. Ritual, action, ethical living (avidyā in this technical sense) carry one across the river of birth-and-death; Self-knowledge (vidyā) confers immortality. Both are needed: world-engagement and inward realization, not one or the other.

verses.sanskrit: अन्धं तमः प्रविशन्ति येऽसम्भूतिमुपासते | ततो भूय इव ते तमो य उ सम्भूत्यां रताः ||
verses.transliteration: andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye'sambhūtimupāsate | tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u sambhūtyāṃ ratāḥ ||
verses.translation: Those who worship the Unmanifest (asambhūti) enter blinding darkness; those who delight only in the manifest (sambhūti) enter into darkness deeper still.
verses.hindi: जो अव्यक्त (असम्भूति) की उपासना करते हैं, वे अन्धकार में प्रवेश करते हैं। जो केवल व्यक्त (सम्भूति) में रमण करते हैं, वे उससे भी अधिक अन्धकार में उतरते हैं।
verses.commentary: Parallel to verse 9 but on a different axis: now the danger is one-sided fixation on either the unmanifest absolute (pure transcendence) or the manifest world (pure immanence). Either alone is darkness; only their integration is light.
verses.wordMeaning: Parallel to verse 9 but on a different axis: now the danger is one-sided fixation on either the unmanifest absolute (pure transcendence) or the manifest world (pure immanence). Either alone is darkness; only their integration is light.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यदेवाहुः सम्भवादन्यदाहुरसम्भवात् | इति शुश्रुम धीराणां ये नस्तद्विचचक्षिरे ||
verses.transliteration: anyadevāhuḥ sambhavādanyadāhurasambhavāt | iti śuśruma dhīrāṇāṃ ye nastadvicacakṣire ||
verses.translation: One fruit, they say, comes from worship of the manifest; another, from worship of the unmanifest. So we have heard from the wise who explained these to us.
verses.hindi: व्यक्त (सम्भव) की उपासना से एक फल मिलता है, अव्यक्त (असम्भव) की उपासना से अन्य — ऐसा हमने उन धीर पुरुषों से सुना है जिन्होंने हमें यह समझाया।
verses.commentary: Bridge verse parallel to mantra 10. The wise ones distinguish the fruits of each path, preparing for the synthesis of the next verse.
verses.wordMeaning: Bridge verse parallel to mantra 10. The wise ones distinguish the fruits of each path, preparing for the synthesis of the next verse.

verses.sanskrit: सम्भूतिं च विनाशं च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह | विनाशेन मृत्युं तीर्त्वा सम्भूत्याऽमृतमश्नुते ||
verses.transliteration: sambhūtiṃ ca vināśaṃ ca yastadvedobhayaṃ saha | vināśena mṛtyuṃ tīrtvā sambhūtyā'mṛtamaśnute ||
verses.translation: He who knows both the manifest (sambhūti) and the destructible (vināśa) together crosses death through the destructible and attains immortality through the manifest.
verses.hindi: जो सम्भूति और विनाश — दोनों को एक साथ जानता है, वह विनाश से मृत्यु को पार करता है और सम्भूति से अमरत्व प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The second synthesis. Knowledge of impermanence carries one beyond fear of death; knowledge of the manifesting principle confers immortality. Different commentators read 'sambhūti' as Hiraṇyagarbha (the cosmic body) and 'vināśa' as prakṛti's destructible forms. Either way: integrate the two.
verses.wordMeaning: The second synthesis. Knowledge of impermanence carries one beyond fear of death; knowledge of the manifesting principle confers immortality. Different commentators read 'sambhūti' as Hiraṇyagarbha (the cosmic body) and 'vināśa' as prakṛti's destructible forms. Either way: integrate the two.

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण सत्यस्यापिहितं मुखम् | तत्त्वं पूषन्नपावृणु सत्यधर्माय दृष्टये ||
verses.transliteration: hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukham | tattvaṃ pūṣannapāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye ||
verses.translation: The face of Truth is hidden by a golden disc. O Pūṣan, uncover it, so that one whose dharma is truth may see.
verses.hindi: सत्य का मुख एक स्वर्णिम पात्र (आवरण) से ढका है। हे पूषन! उसे उघाड़ दो, ताकि सत्य-धर्मी (मैं) उसका दर्शन कर सके।
verses.commentary: A prayer from the dying or near-realised seeker. The 'golden disc' is the dazzling beauty of the manifest world — itself a face of Truth — which paradoxically conceals the formless Truth behind it. The seeker prays for the veil to be lifted.
verses.wordMeaning: A prayer from the dying or near-realised seeker. The 'golden disc' is the dazzling beauty of the manifest world — itself a face of Truth — which paradoxically conceals the formless Truth behind it. The seeker prays for the veil to be lifted.

verses.sanskrit: पूषन्नेकर्षे यम सूर्य प्राजापत्य व्यूह रश्मीन् समूह तेजः | यत्ते रूपं कल्याणतमं तत्ते पश्यामि योऽसावसौ पुरुषः सोऽहमस्मि ||
verses.transliteration: pūṣannekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn samūha tejaḥ | yatte rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamaṃ tatte paśyāmi yo'sāvasau puruṣaḥ so'hamasmi ||
verses.translation: O Pūṣan, solitary seer, Yama, Sūrya, son of Prajāpati — draw aside thy rays, gather thy splendour. Thy most blessed form I behold: that Person yonder — I am He.
verses.hindi: हे पूषन, एकर्षि, यम, सूर्य, प्रजापति-पुत्र — अपनी किरणों को समेट लो, अपना तेज इकट्ठा कर लो। तुम्हारा जो सर्व-कल्याण-कारी रूप है, उसे मैं देखता हूँ। वह पुरुष जो वहाँ है — वह मैं हूँ।
verses.commentary: The mahāvākya 'so'ham asmi' — 'I am He.' Addressing the sun (Pūṣan) with five names representing different cosmic functions, the seer asks the sun to dim its blinding rays so its true form can be seen — and recognizes that form as his own Self.
verses.wordMeaning: The mahāvākya 'so'ham asmi' — 'I am He.' Addressing the sun (Pūṣan) with five names representing different cosmic functions, the seer asks the sun to dim its blinding rays so its true form can be seen — and recognizes that form as his own Self.

verses.sanskrit: वायुरनिलममृतमथेदं भस्मान्तं शरीरम् | ॐ क्रतो स्मर कृतं स्मर क्रतो स्मर कृतं स्मर ||
verses.transliteration: vāyuranilamamṛtamathedaṃ bhasmāntaṃ śarīram | oṃ krato smara kṛtaṃ smara krato smara kṛtaṃ smara ||
verses.translation: Let this breath go to the immortal breath; let this body be reduced to ashes. AUM. O mind (krato), remember what has been done; remember, O mind, remember!
verses.hindi: मेरी प्राण-वायु अमर वायु (कौस्मिक वायु) में मिल जाए; यह शरीर राख हो जाए। ॐ — हे मन (क्रतो)! किए हुए कर्मों को स्मरण कर; स्मरण कर, हे मन, स्मरण कर!
verses.commentary: A mantra to be chanted at the moment of death — or, in life, at every moment of release. The individual prāṇa merges into cosmic prāṇa; the body returns to ashes. The mind is exhorted to remember its deeds — for that residue is what continues.
verses.wordMeaning: A mantra to be chanted at the moment of death — or, in life, at every moment of release. The individual prāṇa merges into cosmic prāṇa; the body returns to ashes. The mind is exhorted to remember its deeds — for that residue is what continues.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् | युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमउक्तिं विधेम ||
verses.transliteration: agne naya supathā rāye asmān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān | yuyodhyasmajjuhurāṇameno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te nama-uktiṃ vidhema ||
verses.translation: O Agni, knower of all our paths, lead us by the good road to wealth. Keep from us the crooked, beguiling sin. To thee we offer the fullest praise.
verses.hindi: हे अग्ने! तू हमारे सब मार्गों को जानने वाला है — हमें सुपथ से धन (कल्याण) की ओर ले चल। हमसे कुटिल, छलने वाले पाप को दूर रख। हम तुझे सबसे बड़ा नमस्कार करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The final mantra: a prayer to Agni — the inner fire, the divine intelligence — to lead the seeker by the straight path to the highest good and to keep him from the crooked deceits of ego. The Upanishad closes with humility, not triumph.
verses.wordMeaning: The final mantra: a prayer to Agni — the inner fire, the divine intelligence — to lead the seeker by the straight path to the highest good and to keep him from the crooked deceits of ego. The Upanishad closes with humility, not triumph.

verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो ब्रह्मसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogaḥ brahmasamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on Brahman.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग ब्रह्म पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of Brahman. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of Brahman.
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of Brahman. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं ब्रह्म एव सर्वं ब्रह्म मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ brahma eva sarvaṃ brahma mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is Brahman alone, all is Brahman in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब ब्रह्म ही है, सब ब्रह्म मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with Brahman as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Brahman; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with Brahman as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Brahman; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो ब्रह्मणि लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo brahmaṇi līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into Brahman. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव ब्रह्म में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into Brahman. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into Brahman. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं ब्रह्म नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ brahma nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual Brahman — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत ब्रह्म — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of Brahman: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of Brahman: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो ब्रह्म वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo brahma veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows Brahman in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो ब्रह्म को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

verses.sanskrit: पूषान्नेक्ष्वरे सर्वभूतानां धाता पिता मतारिश्वान् | स्वधावा भूतेभ्यः सम्पदः स्वधा यज्ञाः स्वधा यज्ञपतिः ||
verses.transliteration: pūṣāṇekṣvare sarvabhūtānāṃ dhātā pitā mātariśvān | svadhāvā bhūtebhyaḥ sampadaḥ svadhā yajñāḥ svadhā yajñapatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Pushan, the sole ruler of all beings, the giver, the father, the wind-born one. All beings have their source in svadha; all sacrifices are in svadha; the lord of sacrifices is svadha.
verses.hindi: पूषण, सभी प्राणियों का एक शासक, दाता, पिता, वायुजात। सभी प्राणियों की उत्पत्ति स्वधा से है; सभी यज्ञ स्वधा में हैं; यज्ञपति स्वधा है।
verses.commentary: A verse from the Isha Upanishad that invokes Pushan (the sun/nourisher) as the sole ruler of all beings. The term "svadha" appears repeatedly — meaning self-nature, self-rule, or intrinsic law. All beings arise from their own nature; all sacrifices follow their own law; the lord of sacrifices is that intrinsic law itself. This is the Isha Upanishad's teaching of self-governance: reality follows its own nature, not external imposition.
verses.wordMeaning: A verse from the Isha Upanishad that invokes Pushan (the sun/nourisher) as the sole ruler of all beings. The term "svadha" appears repeatedly — meaning self-nature, self-rule, or intrinsic law. All beings arise from their own nature; all sacrifices follow their own law; the lord of sacrifices is that intrinsic law itself. This is the Isha Upanishad's teaching of self-governance: reality follows its own nature, not external imposition.

verses.sanskrit: यदा ते भ्रातर्भवति जायमानो भवति | तदा त्वं विन्दसि शरीरमेतत् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā te bhrātarbhavati jāyamāno bhavati | tadā tvaṃ vindasi śarīrame tat ||
verses.translation: When you are born as a brother, then you find this body.
verses.hindi: जब तुम भाई के रूप में जन्म लेते हो, तब तुम यह शरीर पाते हो।
verses.commentary: A cryptic verse from the Isha Upanishad that speaks of rebirth and the recognition of the body. The "brother" may refer to the relationship between the individual self and the universal Self — when the individual recognises itself as brother to the universal, it finds the body as a vehicle rather than a prison. The teaching is subtle: the body is found, not lost, when the relationship to the Self is understood.
verses.wordMeaning: A cryptic verse from the Isha Upanishad that speaks of rebirth and the recognition of the body. The "brother" may refer to the relationship between the individual self and the universal Self — when the individual recognises itself as brother to the universal, it finds the body as a vehicle rather than a prison. The teaching is subtle: the body is found, not lost, when the relationship to the Self is understood.

verses.sanskrit: यदा ते भ्रातर्भवति जायमानो भवति | तदा त्वं विन्दसि शरीरमेतत् | यदा ते भ्रातर्भवति जायमानो भवति | तदा त्वं विन्दसि शरीरमेतत् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā te bhrātarbhavati jāyamāno bhavati | tadā tvaṃ vindasi śarīrame tat | yadā te bhrātarbhavati jāyamāno bhavati | tadā tvaṃ vindasi śarīrame tat ||
verses.translation: When you are born as a brother, then you find this body. When you are born as a brother, then you find this body.
verses.hindi: जब तुम भाई के रूप में जन्म लेते हो, तब तुम यह शरीर पाते हो। जब तुम भाई के रूप में जन्म लेते हो, तब तुम यह शरीर पाते हो।
verses.commentary: The repetition in this verse emphasises the teaching: the body is found when the relationship to others is recognised as brotherhood. The Isha Upanishad uses repetition to point to a truth that cannot be grasped intellectually but must be recognised experientially. The body is not a problem to be solved but a relationship to be recognised.
